title: EvaluateResponse
description: Wire response returned by POST /v1-evaluate. Emitted by atlasent-api/supabase/functions/v1-evaluate/handler.ts. A non-allow decision is NOT an HTTP error; it is a 200 response with decision != 'allow' and (typically) a populated `denial` block.

decision.description: Canonical four-value decision. SDKs MUST handle all four (legacy SDKs that only branched on allow|deny may surface hold/escalate as an error to the caller until they're updated).

permit_token.description: Opaque permit identifier (raw UUID). Present iff decision == 'allow'. Passed back to POST /v1-verify-permit as `permit_token`.

request_id.description: Server-side request identifier. Used as audit deep-link and idempotency key for replays.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the permit expires. Default TTL: 1 hour.

denial.description: Populated on non-allow decisions. Contains the policy-engine reason and a stable code. NOTE: handler.ts currently emits the deny metadata as TOP-LEVEL `deny_code` / `deny_reason` (see below) rather than this nested block; SDKs read both shapes. This nested form is retained for forward/legacy compatibility.

deny_code.description: Top-level stable machine code naming WHY a non-allow decision was reached (e.g. 'SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED', 'OUTSIDE_CHANGE_WINDOW'). This is what handler.ts actually emits today. Pin routing/alerting to this code, not to `deny_reason`. Absent on allow.

signing_hint.description: ADR-055: the binding an approval_artifact.v1 (or approval_quorum.v1) must reproduce for THIS request. Emitted on an INSUFFICIENT_APPROVALS deny, or on an approval-lifecycle escalate, and disclosure-gated by the handler. `bind.action_hash` is computed over the server's enriched context, which a caller cannot recompute, so this is its only source. Absent otherwise.

deny_reason.description: Top-level human-readable explanation accompanying `deny_code`. May change without notice — do not parse it. Absent on allow.

mode.description: Evaluation mode. 'shadow' indicates no permit was minted (request had `shadow: true`).

decisionObject.description: Canonical Decision Object (CDO) — full structured decision record. Optional; absent on shorter responses.

risk_envelope.description: Risk envelope summary. Always present on responses from engine version wire-v1@1.0.0+. The envelope enforces most-restrictive-wins: it can raise severity but structurally cannot soften a deny.

weighted_score.description: Weighted risk score in [0, 1]. Score ≥ 0.70 triggers a hold.

engine_decision.description: Policy engine decision before envelope promotion.

envelope_decision.description: Decision resolved by the risk envelope.

promoted.description: true when envelope_decision is more restrictive than engine_decision.

hard_blocks.description: Deny codes that unconditionally block regardless of score.

factors.description: Per-factor breakdown. Present only when explain=true was passed to the evaluate request.

risk_class.description: Resolved risk class from the evaluation. Present when the risk envelope assigns a class.

authority_basis.description: Why this permit was issued — the authority kind and a reference to the authorizing entity.

kind.description: Authority class that authorized the action.

escalation_id.description: Present iff decision == 'hold'. ID of the HITL escalation auto-created by the control plane. Poll GET /v1/escalations/{id} for resolution.

approval_request_id.description: Present on hold and escalate decisions when the runtime created an approval request (atlasent-api v1-evaluate: every escalate, and approval-gated holds). A person resolves it in the AtlaSent console; poll GET /v1-approvals/{id} and, once approved, claim the single permit with POST /v1-approvals/{id}/claim-permit. Distinct from escalation_id (the HITL escalation). Absent when no approval request was created.

execution_payload_hash_accepted.description: Whether the runtime bound the permit to the caller's own top-level execution_payload_hash (atlasent-api#3355). false = the digest was DROPPED (e.g. a sha256: prefix, or nested under context) and the permit is bound to the runtime's own proof hash, so re-presenting the caller digest at verify yields PAYLOAD_MISMATCH. Absent when the runtime did not report it; SDKs MUST NOT treat absence as true.

human_approval_required.description: Two-stage authorization lifecycle (atlasent-api #1617). Whether this evaluation requires a verified human approval, independent of whether that requirement is currently satisfied — see `human_approval_status`. Absent on responses from a runtime predating this mechanism; SDKs MUST treat absence as unknown, never as false.

human_approval_status.description: Two-stage authorization lifecycle (atlasent-api #1617). Current satisfaction state of the human-approval requirement, distinct from the requirement itself (`human_approval_required`). `rejected` / `expired` / `revoked` are never collapsed into `pending` — each names a distinct reason authority is not presently available. Absent on responses from a runtime predating this mechanism.

permit.description: Wire-format PermitV2 body. Returned alongside `permit_token` when the legacy v1 surface is upgraded to V2.

approval.description: Permit ↔ approval-artifact binding. Present iff /v1-evaluate verified an approval_artifact.v1 for this issuance.
